newsitem.title: USA: FASB weighs restricting "pooling of interests" - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: FASB weighs restricting "pooling of interests" - WSJ.

text.p: The Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) is considering either restricting or putting an end to "pooling of interests" accounting, a popular way to account for large stock mergers, the Wall Street Journal said in Tuesday's electronic edition.

Changes would not take effect until at least 1999, the newspaper said. FASB spokeswoman Deborah Harrington was quoted in the Journal as saying the decision to look at the rules was "a signal that changes are forthcoming that may curtail the use of pooling accounting in the United States."
She was quoted as saying the board wanted to bring U.S. accounting regulations in line with international practices.
